paper.title: Quantum Kibble-Zurek mechanism and critical dynamics on a programmable Rydberg simulator

observable.description: Z2 correlation length xi in lattice sites, from a log-linear fit of the connected correlator G(r) = (1/N) sum_i [<n_i n_i+r> - <n_i><n_i+r>] over the ring

_notes: Ring rather than chain: periodic boundaries make every atom equivalent, so G(r) averages over N identical pairs instead of mixing bulk with ends — and the end bias is worst exactly where xi is largest, which is the regime the experiment probes. a = 5.1 um gives R_b/a = 1.26 at Omega = 2*pi*2 MHz and the FRESNEL_CAN1-class C6, inside the Z2 lobe (1 < R_b/a < 2) and clear of the 5 um minimum trap spacing. The cost of the ring is field of view: R = a/(2 sin(pi/N)) = 45.5 um at N = 56, so N = 96 needs a radius of ~78 um and an SA1-class device — see README.md. expected_max = 28 = N/2 is the largest separation the ring can resolve, a saturation ceiling rather than a prediction. tau_ns stops at 5800 so that tau plus the two 100 ns amplitude edges fits the 6000 ns maximum sequence duration. The register exceeds the radial cap of Pulser's bundled AnalogDevice, so local validation uses the unconstrained MockDevice as a stand-in; validate-emu will reject the spec if the live device is tighter than assumed.
